Fight Serious Charges with an Aggressive Dubuque, IA Drug Distribution Attorney

Drug distribution charges in Dubuque, Iowa, are serious. A conviction can mean prison time, heavy fines, and a record that follows you for life. The stakes are high — and the legal process moves fast.

Henkels & Baker, PC, works with people in Dubuque and the surrounding region who are facing these charges.

Iowa law treats drug distribution as a felony in most cases. That means the state will pursue this aggressively, and you need an experienced drug distribution lawyer by your side.

A charge is not a conviction. How you respond in the early stages matters. The right legal help can shape what happens next. So, whether that means negotiating a reduced charge, challenging the evidence, or building a strong defense before trial, we’re ready to step in and fight for your rights.

If you or someone you care about has been charged with drug distribution in Dubuque, getting legal help now is the most important step you can take.

How Henkels & Baker Approaches Drug Distribution Cases in Dubuque

At Henkels & Baker, PC, we start by reviewing the full facts of your case. How was the evidence gathered? Were your rights respected during the arrest or search?

If law enforcement made errors, that matters. It can change the direction of your case. We look at every charge on the table.

Moreover, drug distribution cases in Iowa often come with added charges such as possession, intent to distribute, or conspiracy. We sort through each one carefully.

Here’s what you’re facing up to if you’re charged with drug distribution in Iowa under Iowa Code § 124.401:

  • Class B Felony: Applies to the distribution of heavy weights of hard drugs, such as over 500g of cocaine, over 1kg of heroin, or more than 50g of fentanyl. It carries up to 25 to 50 years in prison and fines ranging from $5,000 to $1,000,000.
  • Class C Felony: Applies to drugs like marijuana (exceeding 50 kg), smaller amounts of meth or amphetamines, and 100g to 500g of cocaine. It carries up to 10 years in prison and fines from $1,000 to $50,000.
  • Class D Felony: Applies to most other Schedule I, II, or III substances, or counterfeit drugs. This is punishable by up to 5 years in prison and fines between $1,025 and $10,245.
  • Serious Misdemeanor: Applies only to the distribution or delivery of marijuana for no remuneration (giving it away for free) in amounts less than half an ounce. Punishable by up to 6 months in jail and fines up to $1,000.

We do not treat all charges the same way. Some may be reduced. Some may not hold up. Our team also looks at how the case was built. Witness statements, lab reports, and search records all get reviewed. If something does not line up, we find it.

Our goal is to find the best available path forward for you, whether that means negotiating with prosecutors or preparing a firm defense for trial.

Why Dubuque Clients Choose Henkels & Baker for Drug Charges

Choosing the right drug distribution lawyer can shape the outcome of your case. Here is what makes Henkels & Baker, PC the right fit for you:

Criminal Defense Focus Since 2018

Henkels & Baker, PC has been serving clients in Dubuque since 2018. The firm does not dabble in criminal law as a side practice. Drug distribution cases require focused attention.

Our team handles these matters directly, not as an afterthought alongside unrelated legal work. You get lawyers who know Iowa criminal law, not generalists pulled in many directions.

Free Consultations With No Pressure

Every criminal case starts with real questions. We offer free consultations so you can get honest answers before you commit to anything. You talk through your situation openly.

We listen, review the facts, and tell you clearly what we see. No pressure. No sales pitch. Just a direct conversation about your options under Iowa law.

A Small Office That Treats You Like a Person

Our Dubuque office is small by design. With us, you work with a real person who knows your case. When you call, someone who has read your file picks up. That personal attention matters when your freedom is on the line.

Serving Clients Across a 100-Mile Radius

Our firm is based at 40 Main St. in Dubuque, but we serve clients well beyond the city. We cover parts of eastern Iowa, western Wisconsin, and northwestern Illinois. If you live in Dubuque County or the surrounding region, we can help.

Iowa’s drug distribution law applies across our full-service area, and we know those local courts well.

Honest Guidance — Not Overpromising

We tell you the truth about your case. Drug distribution charges in Iowa carry serious penalties. We do not minimize that.

Our job is to carefully review your situation, build a thorough and effective defense, and keep you informed at every step. You will never be left guessing where things stand.

What Happens After a Drug Distribution Charge in Iowa

Drug distribution cases in Iowa follow a clear set of stages. Knowing what comes next can help you stay calm and make smart decisions at each step.

Stage 1: Arrest and Initial Charges

After an arrest in Dubuque County, you will face an initial appearance — usually within 24 hours. A judge sets bail and reads the charges. Iowa Code Chapter 124 governs controlled substance offenses, and distribution charges can range from serious misdemeanors to Class B felonies, depending on the drug type and amount.

As your lawyer, we can review the arrest report, the charging documents, and any evidence right away.

Stage 2: Arraignment

Arraignment happens within a few days of the initial appearance in the Iowa District Court for Dubuque County. You enter a plea — typically “not guilty.” At this stage, we may argue for reduced bail or release conditions. This is also when formal discovery begins.

Stage 3: Discovery and Case Review

Discovery can take four to ten weeks. The state turns over police reports, lab results, search warrant documents, and witness lists. We go over every piece of evidence.

This is where weaknesses in the state’s case often surface, such as illegal searches, chain-of-custody issues, or credibility issues with informants.

Stage 4: Pre-Trial Motions

Your lawyer may file motions to suppress evidence, dismiss charges, or challenge lab findings. Iowa courts consider these motions before trial. A successful suppression motion can lead to reduced charges or even a dismissal.

This stage may last several weeks, depending on the court’s schedule.

Stage 5: Plea Negotiations or Trial

Most cases resolve through negotiation before trial. If a fair deal is not available, the case goes before a judge or jury in the District Court.

Talk to a Drug Distribution Lawyer in Dubuque Today

A drug distribution charge in Iowa can move fast. Do not wait to get legal help. The sooner you reach out, the more options you may have.

At Henkels & Baker, PC, we’re ready to review your case.

Call us, or reach out online to schedule a free initial consultation with our skilled team. Bring any paperwork you have received — charges, court dates, or police reports — so we can explore possible routes.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Can I be charged with drug distribution even if I never sold anything?

Yes — Iowa law allows distribution charges based on possession of a large quantity, packaging materials, or cash, even without a witnessed sale (Iowa Code § 124.401). These are called constructive distribution indicators, and they can trigger serious felony charges.

2. What happens if the drugs are found in a shared space, like a car or apartment?

Prosecutors in Dubuque may charge everyone who had access to that space, but shared access does not automatically prove you had control over the drugs. An experienced drug distribution lawyer can challenge whether the state can prove you knew the drugs were there.

3. Does it matter if the alleged distribution happened near a school or park?

Location matters a great deal under Iowa law — distribution near a school or public park can trigger enhanced penalties that add years to a sentence. These enhanced sentencing zones are a key factor your lawyer should review early in your case.

4. Will a drug distribution charge automatically result in prison time?

Not necessarily. Outcomes depend on the charge level, your prior record, the quantity involved, and how the case is defended. Some first-time defendants in Iowa may qualify for alternative sentencing or diversion programs.

5. How soon should I contact a drug distribution lawyer in Dubuque, IA, after an arrest?

Right away, evidence is collected, and charges are often filed within hours of an arrest. The earlier your lawyer can review the facts, the more options may be available to you.
